**Acute Decompensated Heart Failure (ADHF)** ★★ — Rapid congestion or hypoperfusion at rest: classify perfusion × congestion within ==1 hour==, decongest, never bolus congestion.

- **Typical case:** Dyspnoea + orthopnoea + elevated JVP ★★ (bedside triad).
- **Flow:** Rapid symptoms → classify perfusion × congestion (==1 h==) → IV furosemide (± nitrate if BP allows, NIV if acidosis/hypoxaemia) → reassess ==2 h== & ==6 h== → poor response / urine Na ==<50 mmol/L== → add thiazide.

## Profiles (vs)

| Profile | Mechanism | First-line action |
|---|---|---|
| **Warm + wet** | Congestion, adequate output | Diurese + vasodilate |
| **Cold + wet** ★ | Low output + congestion | Diuretics + consider inotropes |
| **Warm + dry** | Compensated | ==No decongestion== |
| **Cold + dry** | Hypovolaemic or low output | Assess with echocardiography |

## Numbers

| Variable | Value | Clinical meaning |
|---|---|---|
| BNP | ==>100 pg/mL== | Supports dx (obesity ↓, renal failure ↑) |
| NT-proBNP | ==>300 pg/mL== | Supports dx |
| Furosemide start ★ | ==40 mg IV== | Patient ==not== on diuretics (else double home oral dose) |
| Reassessment | ==2 h==, then every ==6 h== | Urine output + symptoms; check K⁺ and renal function after every dose change |
| Diuretic resistance ★ | Urine Na ==<50 mmol/L== at ==6 h== | Flat curve until urine Na rises → add thiazide when response is poor after 6 h |

## Treatment & adjuncts

- **Nitrates:** reduce preload; first line ==when blood pressure allows==.
- **NIV:** respiratory distress with acidosis or hypoxaemia.
- **Inotropes:** cardiogenic shock only, ==not for congestion alone==.
- **Monitoring:** check K⁺ and renal function ==after every diuretic dose change== (hypokalaemia/WRF change plan).

## ⚠ Never

- ==Do not give fluids== for low BP that comes with congestion.
- ==Do not stop beta blockers abruptly== ==unless there is shock==.
- ==Do not use inotropes== for congestion alone.

## Buzzword →

- **Cold and wet** → low output + congestion (diuretics + consider inotropes)
- **Flat dose-response curve** → urine Na <50 mmol/L at 6 h = diuretic resistance

## Cards

- Bedside triad of ADHF → Dyspnoea, orthopnoea, elevated JVP
- How do obesity and renal failure affect BNP (>100 pg/mL)? → Obesity lowers BNP; renal failure raises BNP
- Starting IV furosemide dose in ADHF → 40 mg IV if not on diuretics; double the home oral dose if already taking furosemide
- When to add a thiazide in ADHF → When response is poor after 6 hours (urine Na <50 mmol/L at 6 h predicts resistance)
- When are inotropes indicated in ADHF? → Cardiogenic shock, not for congestion alone
- Can you give fluids for low BP with congestion? → No; do not give fluids for hypotension that comes with congestion
- When is it acceptable to stop beta blockers abruptly in ADHF? → Only when there is shock; do not stop abruptly unless there is shock
